AuthoritativeRule.description:
A domain rule the pipeline (and downstream graders) must treat
as ground truth. Examples: 'final radiology overrides preliminary',
'apixaban dose reduction requires ≥2 of age≥80, weight≤60, Cr≥1.5'.

statement.description: The rule itself, as a single declarative sentence.
statement.title: Statement

applies_to.description: Optional scope: task IDs or document categories the rule binds. Empty = applies globally.
applies_to.title: Applies To

AuthoritativeRule.title: AuthoritativeRule

CanonicalFacts.description:
Core facts the expert fixed in stone. Downstream generation must
preserve these verbatim. Domain-specific sub-fields are all optional
— fill only what your domain needs; use `domain_specific` for anything
not covered.

medications.description: Medical only: canonical med list with any designed discrepancies.
medications.title: Medications

lab_values.description: Medical only: lab / vital values with reference ranges.
lab_values.title: Lab Values

specialist_conflicts.description: Interpersonal disagreements with attending/judge decisions. Medical: specialist-vs-specialist. Legal: State-vs-Defense.
specialist_conflicts.title: Specialist Conflicts

embedded_conflicts.description: Source-document contradictions with a ground-truth resolution. E.g. 'ED prelim CT 4.8 cm vs final radiology 5.2 cm; final authoritative'.
embedded_conflicts.title: Embedded Conflicts

case_law.description: Legal only: statutes + case law that apply to the scenario.
case_law.title: Case Law

domain_specific.description: Escape hatch for anything not covered above. Any domain-specific facts the expert wants the pipeline to respect. Free-form JSON.
domain_specific.title: Domain Specific

CanonicalFacts.title: CanonicalFacts

applicability.description: How this applies to the world's scenario.
applicability.title: Applicability

EmbeddedConflict.description:
Contradiction between two source documents (or two passages
within the same document) with a ground-truth resolution. Distinct
from SpecialistConflict — this is about *documentation* inconsistency,
not interpersonal disagreement. Example: ED prelim CT reads 4.8 cm
vs final radiology reads 5.2 cm; final is authoritative.

authoritative.description: Which source is ground truth (e.g. 'source_b — final radiology authoritative').
authoritative.title: Authoritative

EmbeddedConflict.title: EmbeddedConflict

FileManifestEntry.description: A single document in the world.

format.description: File format the pipeline should render / emit.
format.title: Format

author.description: Party name authoring this doc, if any.
author.title: Author

trap_content.description: What deliberate distortion this file carries, if any. Kept separate from description so the pipeline can distinguish the trap mechanism from the clinical/factual surface.
trap_content.title: Trap Content

reference_docs.description: Authored exemplars the formatter should mirror. A file may cite multiple references — e.g. a template PDF plus prose modifications, or a sample URL plus a backup file. Each entry can be a URL, an uploaded file, or prose-only guidance when no template exists.
reference_docs.title: Reference Docs

for_tasks.description: Task IDs that use this file, e.g. ['T1', 'T2'].
for_tasks.title: For Tasks

label.description: Key = relevant to at least one task or carries a trap. Supplementary = included for realism / completeness only. Mirrors the Label column in the expert File Inventory.
label.title: Label

FileManifestEntry.title: FileManifestEntry

HiddenFinding.description:
A conclusion no single document in the world correctly states —
the model under test must synthesize it across files. Mirrors the
'Hidden Clinical Findings' pattern in medical specs (Elena §1.6)
and the 'Key Factual Tensions' pattern in legal specs (World 1 §1.4).

finding.description: The correct conclusion the model should reach.
finding.title: Finding

evidence_chain.description: The cross-document path to the conclusion — names the specific files / rows / notes that must be combined.
evidence_chain.title: Evidence Chain

HiddenFinding.title: HiddenFinding

InventedFactsPolicy.description:
Rules governing what the pipeline can fabricate vs. what must
come verbatim from source references. Medical worlds typically
allow demographics/admin fabrication but forbid clinical-value
fabrication; legal worlds allow party-backstory fabrication but
forbid statute or case-law fabrication.

allowed.description: Categories the pipeline MAY invent. One per line. E.g. 'patient_demographics', 'address_details', 'witness_backstory', 'transaction_dates'.
allowed.title: Allowed

prohibited.description: Categories the pipeline MUST NOT invent — must come from canonical_facts or referenced source docs. E.g. 'lab_values', 'medication_doses', 'statute_text', 'case_law_holdings'.
prohibited.title: Prohibited

notes.description: Free-form policy guidance (e.g. 'never fabricate clinical values; always fail loud on contradiction').
notes.title: Notes

InventedFactsPolicy.title: InventedFactsPolicy

designed_discrepancy.description: If this entry encodes a trap, note what's deliberately wrong and why.
designed_discrepancy.title: Designed Discrepancy

Party.description:
A character / persona / entity in the world (provider, attorney,
patient, opposing counsel, etc.).

organization.description: Hospital / firm / agency this party belongs to.
organization.title: Organization

representation.description: Legal-only: whose side this party represents (e.g. 'State', 'Defense', 'Neutral'). Leave blank outside legal.
representation.title: Representation

style_guide.description: Per-party voice/formatting conventions for their docs.
style_guide.title: Style Guide

Party.title: Party

ProseRef.description:
Prose-only reference — guidance for the formatter without a
specific template file or URL. Matches expert specs that say
'use standard Orange County arrest report layout' or 'include
measurements showing window position at time of shooting' without
pointing at any template.
ProseRef.title: ProseRef

SpecialistConflict.description:
Interpersonal disagreement between two parties — medical:
specialist-vs-specialist with attending decision. Legal: State-vs-
Defense with judge ruling. For source-document contradictions
(e.g. preliminary radiology vs final), use EmbeddedConflict instead.

trap_id.description: Trap this conflict encodes, if any.
trap_id.title: Trap Id

SpecialistConflict.title: SpecialistConflict

Task.description:
A reasoning task the model under test must solve. Every world
that ships as a benchmark should have at least one. Simple worlds
that exist for content generation only may leave this empty.

anchor_point.description: Temporal grounding — when in the case does this task occur? Medical: e.g. 'Day 8', 'Post-discharge'. Legal: e.g. 'Pre-trial', 'After discovery cutoff'. Constrains which files the agent may see.
anchor_point.title: Anchor Point

capabilities_tested.description: Benchmark skill tags, e.g. 'Medication Safety', 'Synthesis', 'Temporal Reasoning'. Used by downstream graders to categorize.
capabilities_tested.title: Capabilities Tested

file_access_limit.description: Optional constraint on which files the agent may access. E.g. 'No post-discharge files', 'Only files dated before 2024-01-01'.
file_access_limit.title: File Access Limit

design_purpose.description: The correct reasoning path stated plainly — what the agent SHOULD do. Keep separate from the trap so graders see intent.
design_purpose.title: Design Purpose

trap_summary.description: Which trap(s) this task surfaces, and how failure looks.
trap_summary.title: Trap Summary

Task.title: Task

TimelineEvent.description:
A dated event in the world's history. Medical: clinical-event
timeline. Legal: discovery / filing / hearing calendar.

date.description: ISO 8601 or relative label (e.g. '2026-04-14', 'Day 0', '-14 days'). Use absolute when possible.
date.title: Date

source_document.description: Filename (from file_manifest) that documents this event.
source_document.title: Source Document

trap_marker.description: Trap ID activated or anchored on this date, if any.
trap_marker.title: Trap Marker

TimelineEvent.title: TimelineEvent

Trap.description:
A deliberate flaw / ambiguity / contradiction the model under
test is supposed to catch. Mirrors the expert's Trap Activation
Matrix: a first-class declaration, cross-referenced by files
(FileManifestEntry.trap_content) and medications
(MedicationFact.designed_discrepancy) that carry it.

id.description: Stable short name, e.g. 'apixaban-dose-error'. Same ID used as cross-reference elsewhere.
id.title: Id

description.description: The trap mechanism, captured in the expert's own words. Multi-sentence prose is expected and correct — preserve verbatim from the spec, do NOT compress to a one-liner. For prose-shaped traps (multi-step logical, authority-hierarchy, cross-document inference) this is the source of truth that downstream agents (generator, cert checkers, repair) read directly. For phrase-shaped traps a one-line summary is fine if that's what the expert wrote, but never truncate richer explanations.
description.title: Description

carrier_files.description: Filenames of the documents that manifest the trap. Pointer list — tells downstream agents WHERE to look for the trap while `description` tells them WHAT it is. Should match FileManifestEntry.filename values.
carrier_files.title: Carrier Files

affected_tasks.description: Task IDs the trap affects, e.g. ['T1', 'T3']. Cheap pointer list — use this for prose-only traps where you don't want to enumerate per-task misleads/fails/remediation. If you ALSO populate per_task_behavior, the task_ids should agree.
affected_tasks.title: Affected Tasks

per_task_behavior.description: OPTIONAL structured per-task breakdown. Only populate when the expert provided per-task content explicitly (e.g. legacy Task N Traps tab). For prose-shaped traps, leave this empty and rely on `description` + `affected_tasks` — downstream agents read the prose. Each entry ties this trap to a task with its own misleads / failure / remediation.
per_task_behavior.title: Per Task Behavior

must_contain.description: OPTIONAL phrase list. Only populate when the trap is genuinely phrase-shaped (e.g. 'doc A must say 9mm') AND the expert wrote those phrases. Leave empty for logical / multi-step / authority-hierarchy traps — the description carries the meaning and the generator interprets it directly.
must_contain.title: Must Contain

must_not_contain.description: OPTIONAL phrase list — same caveat as must_contain. Phrases that would defuse a phrase-shaped trap. Leave empty for prose-shaped traps.
must_not_contain.title: Must Not Contain

Trap.title: Trap

TrapTaskBehavior.description:
Per-task breakdown of how a trap manifests. Matches the Task N
Traps tab layout in the expert companion spreadsheet.

what_misleads.description: What the document surface suggests that sends agents down the wrong path.
what_misleads.title: What Misleads

how_agent_fails.description: The wrong conclusion an unprepared agent reaches.
how_agent_fails.title: How Agent Fails

remediation_path.description: The correct reasoning path that catches the trap.
remediation_path.title: Remediation Path

TrapTaskBehavior.title: TrapTaskBehavior

description:
Expert-authored world specification. Persistent — edit and
rerun keep the same spec (and its notes). Stored on the
PipelineRun as a snapshot at submit-time.

target_app.description: Which app converter runs after generation. Required per SPL_GUIDE.md — never inferred for production worlds. openemr = medical EHR conversion; clio = legal case mgmt conversion; none = ship raw documents only, skip app conversion.
target_app.title: Target App

summary.description: One-paragraph narrative overview of the case.
summary.title: Summary

tasks.description: Task inventory. Required for benchmarks; optional for content-only worlds.
tasks.title: Tasks

canonical_facts.description: Domain-shaped canonical-fact tables (medications, labs, case law, etc.).

authoritative_rules.description: Domain rules the pipeline and graders must enforce as ground truth (e.g. 'final radiology overrides preliminary', 'apixaban dose reduction requires ≥2 of age≥80, weight≤60, Cr≥1.5').
authoritative_rules.title: Authoritative Rules

invented_facts_policy.description: Rules for what the pipeline may/may not fabricate.

invented_facts_seed.description: Optional seed facts the pipeline should invent around (one fact per line).
invented_facts_seed.title: Invented Facts Seed

global_style_guide.description: Formatting conventions that apply to all documents.
global_style_guide.title: Global Style Guide

pre_flight_notes.description: Free-text guidance for the pipeline — constraints, known gotchas, non-obvious invariants. Persists across reruns.
pre_flight_notes.title: Pre Flight Notes

builder_decisions.description: What the pipeline is free to invent vs. what the spec fixes. Mirrors the 'Builder Decisions Required' section in expert legal specs — names the degrees of freedom (dates, names, measurements, identifiers) so generation doesn't drift.
builder_decisions.title: Builder Decisions

practice_area.description: Legal only: determines document universe and procedural rules.
practice_area.title: Practice Area

procedural_stage.description: Legal only, e.g. 'discovery', 'pre_trial_motions', 'trial', 'sentencing', 'appeal'. Changes which tasks are live.
procedural_stage.title: Procedural Stage

reference_laws.description: Legal only: statutes + case law (URLs or uploaded files).
reference_laws.title: Reference Laws

patient.description: Medical only: narrative patient identity + PMH + baseline labs + allergies + code status + POA. Prose, not JSON — this mirrors how experts write the Patient Profile section in real specs and the pipeline expands it into the PMH sections of every generated document.
patient.title: Patient

care_team.description: Medical only: narrative provider roster (name, role, service, credentials). Cross-referenced when generating notes so authorship stays consistent.
care_team.title: Care Team

specialist_friction.description: Medical only: points of disagreement between services — consults that declined, recommendations that got overruled, plans that persisted without cancellation.
specialist_friction.title: Specialist Friction

clinical_course.description: Medical only: day-by-day narrative of what happens in the world. Anchor events to dates or hospital-day numbers — timeline QC relies on internal consistency here.
clinical_course.title: Clinical Course

clinical_settings.description: Medical only: orgs involved (ED, ICU, clinic, floor, etc.).
clinical_settings.title: Clinical Settings

case_summary.description: Legal only: narrative of the matter — charges, parties, procedural posture, what's in dispute. Grounds every generated filing.
case_summary.title: Case Summary

factual_tensions.description: Legal only: points of factual dispute between parties — the conflicting-document stuff the model must reason across.
factual_tensions.title: Factual Tensions

hidden_findings.description: Conclusions no single document in the world correctly states — the model must synthesize them across files. Each item is the correct conclusion plus the cross-document evidence chain.
hidden_findings.title: Hidden Findings

title: WorldGenSpec
